verdict.rationale: dlt's core product is an open-source Python library. You install it with pip and run it wherever Python runs: a laptop, Airflow, Dagster, Lambda, a container. That makes the core library fully self-hostable, and community users confirm adding it to their own stacks. missing for 10: no evidence that the dltHub managed layer (Web UI monitoring, `dlthub deploy`, managed orchestration) can be self-hosted, and no explicit license terms in the pack.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: dlt is an open-source Python library that loads data from various, often messy data sources into well-structured datasets.
Write the pipeline in Python and run it wherever Python already runs: a laptop, a notebook, Airflow, Dagster, a Lambda, a container.
Be it a Google Colab notebook, AWS Lambda function, an Airflow DAG, your local laptop, or an AI coding agent—dlt can be dropped in anywhere.
it is light enough to be easy to add to a pre-existing data stack.
